soft_launch.subject: You have a new tool. Try it before anyone else.
body: Ask MMT is live in your Premium dashboard as of this morning, a week before it goes public.

It's a research assistant built on two things: live federal data (SAM.gov, USASpending, Congress.gov, and PubMed among them) and the MMT article archive. Ask it about a contract, a vehicle, an agency, a budget line, or a trend. It answers in seconds and shows you where the answer came from.
Three to try:
- What's the status of CCN Next Gen?
- Who are the incumbents on T4NG2?
- What's moving in DHA's FY2027 IT budget?
Then ask it the one you actually need answered this week.

Two things to know. It's research, not a bid decision, so check the sources it hands you. And your monthly question to me hasn't gone anywhere. That's now called Analyst Q&A, and it's still in the dashboard.
If Ask MMT fumbles a question this week, reply here and tell me. You're the first people using it, and that's how it gets better before everyone else sees it.
Talk soon,
Mary

welcome.subject: Your three questions
body: You asked Ask MMT something and it showed you where the answer came from. That's the whole idea.
You have {{FREE_CAP}} questions a month, free. They reset on the 1st.

What it reads: SAM.gov, USASpending, Congress.gov, PubMed, and every MMT article, plus the rest of the list at missionmeetstech.com/ask/sources. If the answer isn't in those systems, it tells you it doesn't know instead of guessing.
What to ask next: the question your pipeline review is going to ask you.
You're also now on the Tuesday and Friday list. Federal health IT analysis, no sponsors, unsubscribe anytime.
Talk soon,
Mary

welcome.subject: One question before you spend B&P
body: Most B&P money gets wasted on pursuits that should have died at the first gate.
Try this with one of your free questions: "Who currently holds [program], when does it expire, and what did the last award look like?"

If the answer shows a strong incumbent, a recent extension, and a sole-source justification, you just saved a red team. If it shows a re-compete window and a thin obligation history, you found something.
Either way, you'll see the SAM.gov and USASpending records it used. That's the part to put in front of your leadership.
Talk soon,
Mary

welcome.subject: Nobody pays for the answer
body: Ask MMT reads federal sources and MMT's own archive. That's it. No vendor content, no sponsored research, no "partner" data.

That matters more than it sounds. Most free federal IT media is funded by the vendors it covers. When you ask a question about a vehicle, you want an answer that wasn't shaped by whoever bought the ad.
MMT is reader-funded. The subscription pays for the independence, and the independence is why the answers are worth checking.
Talk soon,
Mary

body: You've had Ask MMT for almost two weeks. If it's answered something you would have spent an hour on, here's the math.

$29.99 a month, or $249 a year, gets you {{CAP_PREMIUM}} questions a month plus the rest of Premium: the Capture Intelligence sheets with action windows, the agency org charts, the Contract and IDIQ trackers, the Pursuit Calendar, early access to every analysis, and a question a month to me directly.

If this isn't the moment, nothing changes. Your {{FREE_CAP}} questions come back on the 1st.
